root_cause_label: SSH host key generation omitted; no end-to-end SSH connectivity verified before claiming completion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent configured SSH password authentication and restarted sshd but never ran ssh-keygen -A to generate host keys nor verified actual client SSH connectivity, leaving the test harness unable to complete a git-over-SSH operation on a fresh container.
t_err_evidence: The agent's initial plan in step 1 lists all required actions (install packages, create user, init repo, configure sshd, set up nginx) but never mentions generating SSH host keys (ssh-keygen -A) or verifying SSH connectivity from a client; the knowledge gap is embedded in the plan from the very first step.
t_commit_evidence: At step 18 the agent restarts sshd (service ssh restart) after configuring PasswordAuthentication; host keys have still not been generated and the agent proceeds to nginx/verification steps without any SSH connectivity test, locking in the missing host-key failure.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the operational knowledge that on a fresh Ubuntu container the SSH host keys may need to be explicitly generated with ssh-keygen -A before sshd can accept client connections, and that the test client requires known_hosts or StrictHostKeyChecking=no to connect without interactive prompting.
